function.name: introduction_greet
function.description: Generate a greeting message introducing a person and their relationship to another individual. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The name of the person being introduced.

relationship.description: The type of relationship to the related person.

related_person.description: The name of the person to whom the first person is related.

include_relationship.description: A flag to indicate whether to include the relationship in the greeting message.

message.content: I’m just a virtual assistant, so I don’t personally know anyone named Daniel. If you’re asking about a public figure—say, a politician, artist, or athlete—just let me know which Daniel you mean and I’ll see what information I can share.
message.reasoning: User asks: "do you know Daniel?" We need to respond appropriately. According to policy, we should not claim personal knowledge or familiarity with private individuals. We can say we don't personally know them. But we might ask clarifying question: "Which Daniel?" Or we could provide general info about common names. But user didn't specify context. So we should respond politely: "I don't personally know anyone named Daniel." Possibly ask if they want info on a public figure. Also mention privacy. So answer: "I'm an AI; I don't personally know people. If you're referring to a public figure, let me know which one." That satisfies.
